hero.h1: Miami UI/UX design services for products used in English and Spanish
hero.sub: Miami UI/UX design services from a remote-first team headquartered in Reston, Virginia: user research, user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) design and usability testing for fintech and crypto platforms, travel and hospitality brands and real estate companies from Brickell to Coral Gables and across Miami-Dade County, Florida, whose products serve users in the US and Latin America. We work an Eastern Time schedule, the same time zone as Miami.

summary: Remote-first Miami UI/UX design services for fintech, travel, hospitality and real estate teams whose products serve English- and Spanish-speaking users.

sections.h2: What makes UX design for Miami products different?
sections.answer: For Miami products, a remote-first UI/UX design company has to plan for two languages, several countries and a mix of residents, visitors and international buyers in one release. That changes user research recruiting, content planning and how layouts handle longer text.
sections.body: Our remote-first UX design agency sits within the wider field of UI UX design services. We have no Miami or Florida office and work an Eastern Time schedule from Reston, Virginia, the same time zone as Miami. Products that sell into Latin America can need English and Spanish, several currencies and local payment methods, so layouts are planned for both languages from the first wireframe. See our UX research services.

sections.h2: What can a Miami team hand off to us?
sections.answer: Our remote-first UX design agency can take on 6 types of work from a Miami team, either combined into one project or booked one at a time alongside an in-house design team.

items.title: User research.
items.body: Remote user interviews and analytics for each user group, for example South Florida residents, visitors and overseas buyers, recruited from your customer list or a recruitment panel.

items.title: UX audit.
items.body: A heuristic usability review plus a Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) check against WCAG 2.2 level AA, with findings ranked by impact and effort; the UX audit ends with a prioritized fix roadmap.

items.title: Onboarding and KYC flows.
items.body: Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification, wallet setup and funding steps designed to reduce abandonment without weakening compliance.

items.title: Booking and reservation UX.
items.body: Search, availability and checkout for hotels, cruises and experiences, including add-ons and itinerary changes.

items.title: Responsive UI design.
items.body: Mobile-first screens in Figma with a visible language switch and room for longer Spanish strings, which your translators or localization team supply, for example a condo pre-construction showcase with floor plans.

items.title: Usability testing.
items.body: Moderated remote sessions with 5–8 participants per round for each user group, with design fixes between rounds.

sections.h2: When should a Miami company bring in a UX partner?
sections.answer: At 5 moments, South Florida companies can bring in a remote-first UX firm Miami teams can brief within their own working day:
items: Before adding a Spanish version to a product that was designed in English only.
When a fintech or crypto app sees new users drop out during identity verification or the first deposit.
Ahead of the busiest booking season, when booking friction costs the most revenue.
When a real estate brand needs one site that serves local buyers and international investors.
After a funding round, when the product must grow faster than the design team can hire.

sections.h2: How does a Miami project move from brief to build?
sections.answer: Our remote-first UX design agency moves a research and design sprint from kick-off to developer handoff in 4–8 weeks, across 5 stages staffed by 2–4 designers, and every review sits inside Miami's Eastern Time working day.

items.title: Kick-off call (1–2 days)
items.body: We confirm the users, flows, success metrics, markets and languages in scope.

items.title: Learn from users (5–10 days)
items.body: We study each user group the product serves through user interviews, analytics and an expert review, then rank the opportunities we find by impact.

items.title: Direction workshop (2–3 days)
items.body: Remote sessions settle the core flows and content rules; on-site workshops in South Florida can be added for larger engagements.

items.title: Design in detail (10–20 days)
items.body: User flows, interface screens and an interactive prototype in Figma, with the Spanish strings your team supplies loaded so layouts are checked against longer text; progress is shared twice a week.

items.title: Prove and ship (5–10 days)
items.body: Real users try the prototype in one last usability testing round; once the design holds up, your engineers get annotated specs and components.

sections.h2: Bilingual-ready vs English-only design for Miami products
sections.answer: For South Florida products, a remote-first UX design agency plans bilingual-ready design from the first wireframe, while English-only design adds Spanish later and reworks screens. In bilingual-ready design, layouts, formats and research cover English- and Spanish-speaking users before build; the table compares the two approaches area by area.

sections.h2: Miami UX design pricing and budgets
sections.answer: Our remote-first Miami UI/UX design services cost $5,000–$15,000 for a focused 2–3 week UX audit and $25,000–$60,000 for a 4–8 week research and design sprint. Price moves with the flows in scope, the platforms, how deep the user research goes, the number of user groups (for example English- and Spanish-speaking users) and whether a design system is included.
sections.body: A full design engagement that includes a design system costs $60,000–$180,000 over 8–16 weeks; an embedded design team is $15,000–$40,000 a month. A free consultation comes first, followed by a fixed-scope proposal. For scope detail, see UX audit services and usability testing services, or the TradeZella case study for a trading product.

sections.h2: Which Miami industries do we design for?
sections.answer: Our remote-first UX design agency focuses on four sectors well represented in Miami and South Florida:
items: Fintech, payments, remittances and crypto, for example cross-border transfers, business banking, wallets and exchanges (Finance UI UX design), and play-to-earn products like the one in our Nitro case study.
Travel, cruise and hospitality, for example booking engines, loyalty programs and guest apps.
Real estate and proptech, for example luxury listings, pre-construction sales to international buyers and rental platforms.
Consumer and e-commerce brands, for example online stores selling into US and Latin American markets (E-commerce UI UX design).

sections.h2: Questions about Miami UI/UX design services
sections.answer: These five answers cover common questions South Florida product, marketing and founder teams can put to a remote-first UI/UX design company before they commit to a Miami UI/UX project.

faqs.q: Do you have a Miami office?
faqs.a: No. Our remote-first UX design agency is headquartered in Reston, Virginia, without a Miami or Florida office. Kick-off calls, reviews and research sessions run over video on an Eastern Time schedule, the same time zone as Miami, and on-site workshops in South Florida can be added for larger engagements. The UI UX design Miami teams can buy from us starts with user research and continues through interface design and usability testing, with fixed-scope pricing from $5,000. When you shortlist top Miami UX design companies, compare time to start, team size, user research depth and cost model.

faqs.q: Can you design a product for English- and Spanish-speaking users?
faqs.a: Yes. We plan layouts, navigation, a visible language switch and per-country formats for both languages from the first wireframe, and load the Spanish strings your translators or localization team supply into the prototype, so text length is checked before build.

faqs.q: Can you design for crypto and fintech startups?
faqs.a: Yes. Fintech and crypto founders can hire us for trust signals, onboarding with identity verification, and error recovery, while their legal team stays in charge of disclosures and licensing requirements. See Finance UI UX design.

faqs.q: Can user research include customers outside the US?
faqs.a: Yes. Remote user interviews and usability tests run over video, and participants come from your customer list or a recruitment panel, screened to match each user group.

faqs.q: How soon can a Miami UI/UX project start?
faqs.a: Work on a Miami UI/UX project begins 1–2 weeks after proposal approval, with a kick-off call that confirms the users, flows, success metrics and languages in scope. At the end of a sprint you receive research findings, Figma files, an interactive prototype tested with real users, and annotated specs and components; a UX audit delivers a prioritized fix roadmap.
